reader.requirement: At 1985, after an indexed WRITE (with FROM identifier-1, identifier-1 a data item or, per Amendment 1, an alphanumeric function-identifier) completes, identifier-1's content must still be available unchanged, while record-name-1's area is available only through the SAME RECORD AREA clause; the witness covers only a sequential file and an alphanumeric working-storage identifier.

edition-consulted.switches: Constructs.FromLiteral2002: FROM literal-1 (figurative included) refused below 2002 (COBOL0871)

reader.edition-search: grep Edition|CobolVersion|DialectLevel|DialectBehavior over KeyedIoEmitter.cs EmitWrite, SequentialIoEmitter.cs Begin/End/EmitReleasedRecordAlsoAvailable, FileControlBinder.IoControl.cs LinkSameRecordArea and FileModel.SameRecordAreaPeers: none; the SAME RECORD AREA overlay (implicit redefinition) and the out-of-line store are edition-free. The only edition gate on WRITE ... FROM is the 2002 literal operand.
reader.behaviour-differs-by-edition: no: the also-available mechanism is one arm; only FROM literal-1 is an edition arm (refused at 85)
reader.witnesses-cover: part: l1c37 covers sequential files and a PIC X working-storage identifier; not exercised: indexed record-name-1, COMP-3/edited identifier-1, a function-identifier (Amendment 1), FROM a peer record (SR1 refusal)

probes.printed: indexed RANDOM F1 + sequential F2 + indexed DYNAMIC F3 in one SAME RECORD AREA: W1 OK 00; SRC K01 -123 TAIL; R1 K01 -123 TAIL; R1B K01 TAIL; R2 K01|TAIL; R3 K01 TAIL; dup-key WRITE -> W2 IK 22, R2 still K01; WRITE R3 FROM edited-pic item -> W3 OK 00, ED -12.50, R1/R2 show -12.50; reread RD1 K01 -123 TAIL 00, RD3 -12.50 00
probes.expected: after a successful WRITE the record stays in record-name-1's area and is available as every peer file's record (GR2); identifier-1 (WS-SRC with COMP-3, WS-ED edited) keeps its content (GR4)

probes.printed: RECORD VARYING 4..12 + ODO indexed SEQUENTIAL record sharing with an elementary numeric record (out-of-line) and an indexed group: W1 OK 00, C 4 T AB RL 06, R3 1234ABCD, WS 1234ABCD; W2 00 R3 5550ABCD; WRITE R2 (S9(11)V9 SIGN SEPARATE) -> R3 012345678905+ K1 012; reread RD 1234AB 06 / 5550 04
probes.expected: variable-length released record and out-of-line elementary peer both see the released record (GR2); FROM operand unchanged (GR4)

probes.printed: WRITE R3 FROM WS-Z ('000000012345+') -> W4 00; MOVE R2 TO edited -> 1234.5
probes.expected: the indexed file's released record is available as the elementary numeric peer record R2 (GR2)

probes.printed: WRITE R1 FROM FUNCTION UPPER-CASE(WS) -> W1 OK 00, R2 ABCDEFGH, WS abcdefgh; second OPEN I-O -> 41; WRITE after OPEN INPUT -> W3 48, R2 abcdefgh (GR3 a MOVE happened)
probes.expected: 1985 Amendment 1 alphanumeric function-identifier as FROM operand works; failed WRITE (not open for output) unsuccessful

probes.printed: error COBOL0871: FROM literal-1 requires COBOL-2002 (targeting COBOL-85) - WRITE ... FROM literal-1
probes.expected: 1985 FROM takes identifier-1 only; WRITE R1 FROM ZERO refused

probes.printed: error COBOL6827: WRITE FROM R2: the operand names the record area of file 'F1' (§1985:IX.4.9.3 SR1)
probes.expected: a peer record of the same SAME RECORD AREA is the same storage area as record-name-1: refused by SR1

citations.check: OK  §1985:IX.4.9.4 GR4  (4.9.4 General Rules)  the text is in GR4
OK  §1985:IX.4.9.4 GR3  (4.9.4 General Rules)  the text is in GR3

reader.notes: WRITE FROM is MOVE identifier-1 TO record-name-1 then WRITE (GR3); identifier-1 is only read, so it stays available (WS-SRC COMP-3, WS-ED, the UPPER-CASE source all unchanged in probes), and the record area's continued availability goes through the SAME RECORD AREA mechanism. FROM literal-1 is refused at 85 (COBOL0871) and FROM a peer record by SR1 (COBOL6827).

refuter.evidence: refute-1985-011/c3/r1.cob (--std 85, indexed DYNAMIC, group alphanumeric key): WRITE R1 FROM WS-T(K1) with K1 inside the record area: record gets WS-T(2) (subscript evaluated once before the MOVE), table unchanged; WRITE R1 FROM R9 (record of another open indexed file, no SAME RECORD AREA) -> R9 still XQRSTU; WRITE R1 FROM FUNCTION REVERSE(R1) writes edcba3; WRITE R1 FROM WS-N (S9(4) COMP-3 -42, a group move) -> WS-N still -0042, record carries its bytes; reread all four. r2.cob: FROM FUNCTION LENGTH(R9) refused at 85 (COBOL1914 citing §1985:IX.4.9.3 SR1, COBOL0900). OK  §1985:IX.4.9.4 GR4 the text is in GR4.
